correctness.rationale: The independent-copy formula divides by d! and all block lengths. For Gaussian increments each determinant contributes the square roots of the block lengths times a common standard Gaussian determinant; its expectation cancels d! and gives the stated unit-ball factor with the normalized mixed volume. The generating function of F_r is Li_{1/2}(z)^r/(1−z). The first two singular powers are −1−r/2 and −(r+1)/2; transfer gives the asserted leading coefficient and relative correction β_r. The expansion is in a slit domain and can be transferred sufficiently far that log F_r(k), after its leading logarithm, has powers k^{-j/2} through j=5 and remainder O(k^{-3}); thus differencing the remainder does not jeopardize either displayed log-difference estimate. Leading asymptotics give interior maximizers with m/N→p/d, excluding endpoints by the uniform power bound. There the forward increment has leading drift (pN−dm)/(2m(N−m)) with uniform error O(N^{-3/2}). Its forward and backward signs at a maximizer imply |m−pN/d|=O(sqrt N). Expanding there gives slope −d³/(2pq) in the scaled coordinate and zero at the stated α, with uniform O(N^{-2}) increment error, so the location error is bounded in steps. The second log-difference makes the increment strictly decreasing on a common interior interval containing all maxima, excluding three or two nonadjacent maxima. The digamma integrand is e^{−xt/2}/(1+e^{t/2}), strictly bounded by (1/2)e^{−(x/2+1/4)t}; this proves that h decreases and, as ζ(1/2)<0, that β_r/r^{3/2} increases. Hence the bias has sign q−p and vanishes at equality; substitution gives the stated (2,1) example. Replay: RESULT.md lines 37–91, with the precise source normalization below. The supplied verify_budget.py was inspected, not executed, and its finite floating-point estimates are not evidence of an all-large-budget threshold or of exact ties. The proof applies only to fixed p,q and the stated Gaussian walks.
